nodes.description: Owner address of the Owned contract; set in constructor and used as the onlyContractOwner access gate.
Two-step ownership handover slot written by changeContractOwnership and consumed/cleared by claimContractOwnership.
Public token symbol string declared in ERC20Interface.
Mapping(address=>bool) of contracts authorized to emit events through the MultiEventsHistory fallback.
Caller-controlled source address of the transaction.
Constructor that assigns contractOwner = msg.sender.
Owner-only selfdestruct of the contract via suicide(msg.sender).
Owner-only first step of ownership transfer; stores pending owner and rejects 0x0.
Second step of ownership transfer; requires msg.sender == pendingContractOwner then moves owner and deletes pending.
Owner-only loop that transfers any leftover ERC20 balances held by the contract to a destination address.
Internal constant helper returning OK when msg.sender is the contract owner.
Owner-only authorization of a caller contract in the isAuthorized mapping.
Owner-only revocation of a caller contract's authorization.
Unauthenticated fallback of MultiEventsHistory; delegatecalls msg.sender with msg.data when authorized.
opcode suicide/selfdestruct invoked in destroy() with msg.sender as beneficiary.
msg.sender.delegatecall(msg.data) executed inside the fallback, running untrusted code in this contract's storage context.
External ERC20Interface(token).transfer(_to, balance) call performed on an attacker-supplied token array entry.
Destination address parameter of changeContractOwnership.
Caller address parameter of authorize.
Caller address parameter of reject.
Array of token contract addresses passed to withdrawnTokens.
Recipient address parameter of withdrawnTokens.
Loop-local address of the current token contract in withdrawnTokens.
Loop-local ERC20 balance returned by balanceOf(this) in withdrawnTokens.
Loop counter variable in withdrawnTokens.

edges.reason: msg.sender is stored directly into contractOwner in the constructor.
Owned() writes the caller-supplied msg.sender into the contractOwner state variable.
destroy() is guarded by onlyContractOwner, which reads contractOwner.
destroy() invokes the suicide opcode.
msg.sender is passed as the selfdestruct beneficiary, sending all funds to the caller.
changeContractOwnership() is gated by the onlyContractOwner modifier reading contractOwner.
changeContractOwnership receives _to as its destination argument.
The caller-supplied _to is written into pendingContractOwner.
claimContractOwnership compares msg.sender against pendingContractOwner.
claimContractOwnership reads and then deletes pendingContractOwner.
claimContractOwnership promotes pendingContractOwner into contractOwner.
checkOnlyContractOwner reads contractOwner to build its access-control return code.
checkOnlyContractOwner compares contractOwner with msg.sender.
withdrawnTokens() is restricted by the onlyContractOwner modifier.
withdrawnTokens iterates over the tokens address array parameter.
Each element of tokens is copied into the token local variable.
balanceOf(this) result is stored in the balance local variable.
_to is used as the destination of the token transfers in withdrawnTokens.
Loop counter i controls the token iteration in withdrawnTokens.
withdrawnTokens performs an external ERC20 transfer call for each non-zero balance.
The measured balance is the value passed to the external transfer call.
The external call to an attacker-controlled token contract can re-enter withdrawnTokens before it finishes.
authorize() is guarded by onlyContractOwner which reads contractOwner.
authorize receives _caller as the address to authorize.
The caller-supplied _caller becomes an authorized event emitter in isAuthorized.
authorize writes true into the isAuthorized mapping.
reject() is guarded by onlyContractOwner which reads contractOwner.
reject receives _caller as the address to revoke.
reject deletes the isAuthorized entry of _caller.
The fallback checks isAuthorized[msg.sender] to decide whether to proceed.
The fallback reads the isAuthorized mapping to gate its delegatecall.
The fallback executes delegatecall on msg.sender with attacker-controlled msg.data.
msg.sender is the delegatecall target, so the caller chooses the code executed in this storage context.
The delegatecall target can re-enter the payable fallback recursively while msg.data is under attacker control.
